candidates.name: Altes Rathaus & Spielzeugmuseum
candidates.content: This was built in 1474 to replace an even older town hall, and was the city chambers until Neues Rathaus was built in the late 19th century. It was bombed during World War II but rebuilt. It's now mostly a ceremonial hall and even

candidates.name: Peterskirche
candidates.content: Munich's first parish church was started in the 12th century, but burned down in the great city fire of 1327. It was rebuilt by 1368 in Gothic style. The 92 m main tower (called Alter Peter) stands between the stumps of two origin

candidates.name: Frauenkirche
candidates.content: This huge church defines the Munich skyline with its twin onion-domed towers, a shade over 98 m tall - the money ran out for the planned spires. It's the Roman Catholic cathedral, but always known locally as Frauenkirche. It was b

candidates.name: Theatinerkirche
candidates.alt: Church of St Cajetan and Adelheid
candidates.content: Roman Catholic church in eye-catching Italianate High Baroque, looking like it belongs in Syracuse. The Theatins were an austere monastic order founded by the 15th century Saint Cajetan, and they built several similar churches. Th

candidates.name: Residenz
candidates.content: Royal Palace and seat of government of the Wittelsbach dynasty, bombed in wartime but rebuilt. The two principal areas are the Treasury and the Museum (separate admission €9 each). The Treasury (Schatzkammer) has a huge collection

candidates.name: Bayerisches Nationalmuseum
candidates.content: Huge and fascinating museum of European history from the Middle Ages until early 20th century. There's armour, pottery, furniture, fashions, porcelain, beer mugs, the lot; plus Oct-April a display of nativity scenes. The Bollert m

candidates.name: Michaelskirche
candidates.content: Grand Renaissance church built for the Jesuits 1583-1599 by Duke Wilhelm V, as a bastion of the Counter-Reformation against those awful Lutherans. The Duke nearly busted the state coffers in buying up the land and funding a constr

candidates.name: Münchner Stadtmuseum
candidates.content: Extensive museum, occupying most of a city block; absorbing but signage is only in German. The oldest part of the building is an armory of 1500, the newest is the former Uhlfelder department store (all bombed in wartime, but the c

candidates.name: Museum Villa Stuck
candidates.content: Franz von Stuck (1863-1928) was a painter and sculptor best known for his renditions of mythological scenes. From 1897 he designed this neo-classical mansion. There's a permanent display of his own works plus changing exhibitions

candidates.name: Deutsches Museum
candidates.alt: German Museum of Masterpieces of Science and Technology
candidates.content: Enormous museum of science and technology, needing a full day, and even then you need to prioritise which galleries to explore - though half the fun is discovering the secrets of technology you'd never considered. Themes include n

candidates.name: St Maxmilian Church
candidates.content: In a prominent position on the banks of the Isar, this Roman Catholic parish church was mostly complete by 1908, though the sacristry was only added in 1938. It was bombed during wartime but restored by 1953. It was again closed f

candidates.name: Old South Cemetery
candidates.content: This was established in 1563 when plague overfilled the church graveyards, and bodies needed to be interred beyond city limits. St Stephan's church at its main north entrance was built at the same time. From 1788 to 1868 it was Mu

candidates.name: St Paul's church
candidates.content: Massive Roman Catholic church in neo-Gothic style, completed in 1906. It was bombed out in 1944 but rebuilt, albeit with a simpler interior. Its best known feature is the 97 m main tower. In 1960 a Convair C-131 transport plane lo

candidates.name: Palaeontological Museum
candidates.content: Lots of fossils including Archaeopteryx, Triceratops and Saber-toothed Cat. The museum itself is an interesting building, on three floors but an hour is plenty to see it all.

candidates.name: Museum Brandhorst
candidates.content: Opened in 2009, this has a permanent collection of modern and contemporary paintings, sculptures and installations, especially by Andy Warhol and Cy Twombly.

candidates.name: Olympiaturm
candidates.content: This 291 m tower was built in 1968 and looks it: the centrepiece for the 1972 Olympic complex. The revolving restaurant (see below) is at 182 m and the observation deck is at 190 m. Until 2021 it housed a rock and roll museum but

candidates.name: Schloss Nymphenburg
candidates.price: Apr-mid Oct adult €15, conc €13; mid Oct-Mar adult €12, conc €10
candidates.content: What began as a modest 17th century pavilion grew and grew into a vast Baroque palace, bigger than Versailles, which was no accident. You view some 20 ornate rooms: one striking feature is the paintings of the many female friends

candidates.name: Blutenburg Castle
candidates.content: This was built in 1438 as a hunting lodge for Albert III, Duke of Bavaria. It was on a river island between two arms of the River Würm, with the east arm dammed to create an ornamental lake - leisure rather than defence was always

candidates.name: Kunsthalle München der Hypo Kulturstiftung
candidates.content: Modern art museum, no permanent collection but rotating exhibitions. It's funded by HypoVereinsbank.

candidates.name: State Chancellery
candidates.content: This fills the east side of Hofgarten, housing the Bavarian Minister (president of the Lande government) and his / her cabinet meetings. The central dome was built in 1879 to house the Royal Bavarian Army Museum. It was bombed out

candidates.name: Schack Gallery
candidates.content: An extensive private collection of 19th century Late Romantic art.

candidates.name: Jewish Museum
candidates.content: Small museum of Jewish life in the city - and death. It adjoins the Ohel Jakov synagogue and the Jewish community centre.

candidates.name: Asamkirche
candidates.content: This Late Baroque confection was built from 1733 to 1746 as a private chapel by Egid Quirin Asam - he could see the altar from his house next door. His brother, Cosmas Damian Asam, did the frescoes. The church is dedicated to St J

candidates.name: Friedhof Bogenhausen
candidates.content: You need to be influential to earn a plot in this small cemetery. Those that did so include film producer Bernd Eichinger, director Rainer Werner Fassbinder, writer Oskar Maria Graf and writer Erich Kästner. It's by the attractive

candidates.name: Maximilianeum
candidates.content: This is the grand sort-of Renaissance building closing the vista across the Maximilian Bridge, with the road and tramway dividing around it. It was built in fits and starts from 1857 to 1874, the problem being the steep riverbank

candidates.name: Museum of Egyptian Arts
candidates.content: Museum with classical Egyptian antiquities.

candidates.name: Chinese Tower
candidates.content: This 25 m high pagoda was constructed with the original park in 1790, and rebuilt after World War II in 1952. It has a beer garden, with a Bavarian oompah band performing at weekends from the second floor. It can feel touristy, an

candidates.name: Neues Rathaus
candidates.content: This was built in phases from 1867 to 1909. It's still a busy city chambers, with access only on business, but you can ride the lift to the observation deck of the tower. For most visitors the ornate neo-Gothic exterior is experie

candidates.name: Müllers'ches Volksbad
candidates.content: Have a swim at this Art Nouveau public indoor pool opened in 1901 - bring your own towel. The sauna is temporarily closed to save heating costs, and the cafe is closed permanently.

candidates.name: Surfing on the Eisbach
candidates.content: The Eisbach is an artificial side-channel of the Isar, culverted beneath Altstadt but emerging at the bridge on Prinzregentenstraße, south edge of English Garden. Here it drops over a 1 m weir to form a standing wave, surfable whe

candidates.name: Kammerspiele
candidates.content: Avant garde theatre, often with surprising modern interpretations of the classics. Some performances are in English, and all have English subtitles.

candidates.name: Bavarian State Opera
candidates.content: Shows ballet and opera performances almost every night.

candidates.name: Residenztheater
candidates.content: This stages a variety of classical and modern plays.

candidates.name: Staatliches Hofbräuhaus München
candidates.content: This brewery was founded in 1591, and moved to Riem in 1988. They produce over a dozen beers including an Oktoberfest brew. Tours are only available to groups of 10-30, booked at least 14 days in advance.

candidates.name: TSV 1860 Munich
candidates.content: Sechzig ("Sixty") were founder members of Bundesliga, but now play soccer in 3. Liga the third tier. Their stadium (capacity 15,000) also hosts Bayern Munich second team, under-19s and women. Türkgücü München also played here but

candidates.name: Cosima wave pool
candidates.content: This is Munich's only wave pool. It also has a large sauna.

candidates.name: Prinzregententheater
candidates.content: This magnificent Art Nouveau theatre, modelled on the Wagner-Festspielhaus in Bayreuth, houses the Bavarian Drama Academy. The focus of the shows is on opera and musical.

candidates.name: Deutsches Theater München
candidates.content: Grand theatre opened in 1896, the style is called neo-baroque but in this upmarket district the building doesn't greatly stand out. Early fare was music hall, popular comedy and light theatre. Nowadays their programme is mostly mu

candidates.name: Münchner Volkstheater
candidates.content: The theatre left its old venue on Brienner Straße in 2021 and now dwells down near the southside railway tracks. They offer an eclectic mix, often contemporary takes on the classics.

candidates.name: FC Bayern Munich
candidates.content: Die Bayern play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. They do well and qualify for European tournaments, and matches sell out. (Buy tickets online, but you have to register, to curb the touts and scalpers.) The Arena (capacity 70-75

candidates.name: MTTC Iphitos
candidates.content: This is the principal tennis club in Munich. In mid April they host the Bavarian International (sponsored as BMW Open), played over a week on clay. It ranks in the fourth tier of the ATP tournament schedule.

candidates.name: DAV Kletter- und Boulderzentrum
candidates.content: Large indoor bouldering and climbing centre, gets busy out of office hours.

candidates.name: Basketball: FC Bayern Munich
candidates.content: They're better known as a soccer club, but Bayern Munich also play in Basketball Bundesliga, the game's top tier. Their home court is Rudi-Sedlmayer-Halle, sponsored as Audi Dome. It seats 6700 and was built in 1972 for the Olympi

candidates.name: Sugar Mountain
candidates.content: Culture and activity centre in a disused concrete factory. Activities (many free) include fitness classes, bouldering, basketball and skatepark. Culture includes film, concerts, theatre, art exhibitions and warehouse raves. There'

candidates.name: Feierwerk
candidates.content: Cultural centre in a former industrial depot with live music venues (Hansa 39, Kranhalle, Orangehouse, Sunny Red), a radio station (Radio Feierwerk 92.4 ), an artist's workshop (Farbenladen) and a skatepark (Skateplatzl).

candidates.name: Bayern Munich training ground
candidates.content: These pitches host junior teams of Bayern Munich, right down to 8 year olds - so some of them will be star players five or six World Cups from now, imagine. The first team also trains here with a public session at least once a wee

candidates.name: Boulderwelt München Ost
candidates.content: In this large bouldering hall you can test your climbing skills without a harness on 13 different courses. It also has a competition wall, 3 child courses, a bistro, and an outdoor course with slackline park and beer garden in sum

candidates.name: Silberfabrik
candidates.content: A screen-printing workshop and creative space which offers silkscreen and t-shirt printing courses.

candidates.name: P1 Club
candidates.content: Posh nightclub that was once considered a favorite of the high society. Today more lounge than discotheque with a large outdoor terrace. "P1" is shorthand for the address.

candidates.name: Pimpernel
candidates.content: Small nightclub 100 m south of Sendlinger Tor. This venue with red plush and mirrored walls once was a hotspot of Munich's gay scene - a frequent customer was Freddie Mercury who lived nearby. Today it is an afterhours house and t

candidates.name: Forschungsbrauerei
candidates.content: The name means "Research Brewery" and it was established in 1930 to try different brews and test them on customers. The research ended in 1950 and Hopfenhäcker craft brewery now occupies the space. The beer garden is at the edge o

candidates.name: Bahnwärter Thiel
candidates.content: Techno club and alternative cultural centre that resides in graffiti-covered pile of ship containers. The inventory of the club includes many curiosities such as discarded subway cars, trams, construction cranes or carriages. The

candidates.name: Blitz Club
candidates.content: Techno club in the former historic congress hall of the Deutsches Museum. One of the main venues for techno in Munich with a regular international DJ lineup. It also offers a series of gay events called Cruise. Note that the club

candidates.name: Rote Sonne
candidates.content: Legendary techno club, many complaints of aggressive bouncers.

candidates.name: Insel Mühle
candidates.content: As the name indicates, this is a former mill on an island in the river Würm. In summer the 800-seater beer-garden serves Augustiner beer. The hotel and restaurant are open year-round.

candidates.name: Hofbräuhaus
candidates.content: Munich's most famous bräuhaus, here since 1644, is touristy but great fun; you may need photo-ID to get in. Schwemme is the 1300-seater ground floor beer hall in the original brewery area. There's oompah music at weekends - listen

candidates.name: Augustiner Stammhaus
candidates.content: Beer hall and restaurant of Augustiner brewery, founded in 1294, great atmosphere, beer and trad food. They have another beerhall on Arnulfstraße, see Munich/Maxvorstadt#Drink).

candidates.name: Viktualienmarkt beer garden
candidates.content: This is the only beer garden in Altstadt, just south of Marienplatz. With 600 seats, it serves beer from all the big Munich breweries Augustiner, Hacker-Pschorr, Hofbräu, Löwenbräu, Paulaner, and Spaten. It can feel touristy.

candidates.name: Kilians Irish Pub
candidates.content: Kilians is behind the Frauenkirche and offers the usual Irish beers. Friendly place with good beer and grub, occasionally hosts live music, and it's a popular place among expats, tourists, and Germans alike.

candidates.name: Kugleralm
candidates.content: Trad 2400-seater beer garden in Oberhaching south of Perlacher Forst, serving Spaten beer. In 1922 this was the launchpad of the Radler, half beer half lemonade, a "shandy" in English. The legend goes that they were mobbed by cycl

candidates.name: Café im Hinterhof
candidates.content: Hinterhof means courtyard and it's an attractive cafe-bar, with regular piano live music and exhibitions. They offer breakfast / brunch throughout the day and have good cakes.

candidates.name: Café Crönlein
candidates.content: Café-bar in a former public restroom, an odd little stone building that looks more like a park attendant's tool shed. There's more capacity in summer when you can sit outside.

candidates.name: Deutsche Eiche
candidates.content: This hotel restaurant caters to non-residents and gets great reviews. Look for the row of flags, including an LGBT flag to mark the hotel's history in the gay community, and usually a platter of raw mushrooms outside the main entr

candidates.name: Bratwurst Glöckl
candidates.content: Traditional Bavarian restaurant opposite Frauenkirche. Their specialty is Nürnberger Rostbratwürstl - smaller than a standard sausage, so a serving is six instead of the usual three.

candidates.name: Schneider Bräuhaus
candidates.content: Bavarian restaurant and beer garden run by Schneider Weisse, the wheat-beer brewery. Good traditional fare, somewhat cheaper than their more touristy outlet in Altstadt.

candidates.name: Nachtkantine
candidates.content: This restaurant, bar and live music venue is in the works canteen of the former Pfanni factory. They serve burgers, pizza and pasta but get poor reviews for quality and service.

candidates.name: Grano
candidates.content: Good pizza and location, so it can get crowded.

candidates.name: Sasou
candidates.content: This pan-Asian fast food restaurant on the south side of Marienplatz serves excellent Asian noodle soups for an affordable price.

candidates.name: Haxnbauer
candidates.content: This traditional Bavarian restaurant 100 m east of Marienplatz remains closed in 2022.

candidates.name: Tegernseer Tal
candidates.content: Solid traditional Bavarian food and open late, run by Tegernseer Brewery.

candidates.name: Attentat Griechischer Salat
candidates.content: Modern Greek restaurant serving salads, huge portions.

candidates.name: EscoBar
candidates.content: Lively friendly Tex-Mex restaurant near East station.

candidates.name: Il Padrino
candidates.content: Cosy Italian restaurant, good value fare.

candidates.name: L'Angolo della Pizza
candidates.content: Busy place near the station serving Italian staples.

candidates.name: Viktualienmarkt
candidates.content: Large open-air market.

candidates.name: Daseinstein
candidates.content: Shopping centre with Media Markt for electronics, Netto and Edeka supermarkets, a pharmacy, miscellaneous shops and eating places.

candidates.name: Galeria Kaufhof
candidates.content: This chain department store has some eight locations across the city, but the one at Rotkreuzplatz is the most useful for the northwest districts. There's a market hall adjacent.

candidates.name: Dallmayr Delikatessenhaus
candidates.content: A legendary delicatessen store with market and bakery. Its eat-in choices are the cafe-bistro, bar-grill, and restaurant.

december.text: Winters last from December to March. While Munich used to be known for its snow, consistent snow cover is now rare and often melts within a few days. The coldest month remains January, but temperatures frequently hover above freezing. Summers in Munich are warm and pleasant, with an average maximum of 23.8°C (73.8°F) i
Tollwood organise two extended music festivals: June-July in Olympic Park in northern Munich, and Nov-Dec (with a Christmas market) on the Wies'n site in Ludwigsvorstadt.
thumb | 300px | Christmas market at Chinese Tower

Christmas markets (Weihnachtsmarkt or Christkindlmärkt) are held in the four weeks of Advent up to Christmas Eve, offering as much mulled wine, sausage and wood-carved knick-knacks as you can handle. They're typically open daily 12:00 to 20:00. The biggest and most touristy is in Marienplatz in Altstadt, spilling down

The English Garden is the huge park starting just beyond Lehel and described as part of northern Munich. However its southern section is within walking distance, or use U-Bahn U3 or U6 to Universität. is the focal point of this section, a prominent neo-classical rotunda. 200 m further north is the Chinese Tower, with a

Christmas Market is held in Marienplatz in the four weeks to Christmas Eve. Another on Wittelsbacherplatz (by Odeonsplatz) is medieval-themed, so you get to experience how earlier centuries gobbled sausage and slurped mulled wine.

Asamkirche: This Late Baroque confection was built from 1733 to 1746 as a private chapel by Egid Quirin Asam - he could see the altar from his house next door. His brother, Cosmas Damian Asam, did the frescoes. The church is dedicated to St John Nepomuk (1345-93), a Bohemian monk cast into t
East Ice Rink is across the park from the swimming pool and beer garden, on Staudingerstraße.
Haidhauser Weihnachtsmarkt is a Christmas Market held on Weißenburger Platz (100 m east of S- & U-Bahn: Rosenheimer Platz). It's daily from 28 Nov to 24 Dec.

is one of the three surviving (though much altered) gothic city gates: Isartor and Karlstor are the others. In the 13th century the city expanded and needed a new defensive wall and gates. Sendlinger Tor originally had a central tower over a triple gate, and two flanking towers were added in 1420. All this did an excel
thumb | 300px | Tollwood Winter Festival

Tollwood Winter Festival is held on the Wiesn site from late November to Christmas, with music, food stalls and a Christmas Market. Their summer festival is mid-June to mid-July in Olympiapark, see Munich/North#Do.

Pink Christmas is a gay / lesbian Christmas fair on Stephansplatz just south of Sendlinger Tor, from late Nov to Christmas Eve. The name is literal: everything is coloured pink. They put on a live show at 19:00.
Ice skating (Schlittschuhlaufen): in winter the ponds and lakes may freeze hard enough for skating. One popular spot is the ornamental canal in front of Schloss Nymphenburg, directions above.

Tollwood music festivals are twice a year. The summer festival is mid-Jun to mid-July in Olympiapark around the Olympiaberg. The winter festival is on Theresienwiese (the Oktoberfest venue) from the last week of November until Christmas, and includes a Christmas Market.

Christmas fair at the Chinese Tower in English Garden is held from the beginning of December to Christmas Eve, M-F 12:00-20:30, Sa Su 11:00-20:30. It's walking distance from Altstadt, or take U-Bahn U3 or U6 to Universität.
Schwabing Christmas Fair is held at Münchner Freiheit (U-Bahn U3, U6) from late Nov to Christmas Eve, M-F 12:00-20:30, Sa Su 11:00-20:30.

Chinese Tower: This 25 m high pagoda was constructed with the original park in 1790, and rebuilt after World War II in 1952. It has a beer garden, with a Bavarian oompah band performing at weekends from the second floor. It can feel touristy, and horse-drawn carriage and rickshaw tours through

Olympiaturm: This 291 m tower was built in 1968 and looks it: the centrepiece for the 1972 Olympic complex. The revolving restaurant (see below) is at 182 m and the observation deck is at 190 m. Until 2021 it housed a rock and roll museum but this has closed. No reservations for the lift, but

Sendling was a village within walking distance of the city. It's best known for the Sendlinger Christmas Massacre of 1705, when a peasant revolt was crushed with the loss of 1100 lives.
